newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London shares vote to follow U.S. higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London shares vote to follow U.S. higher.

text.p: Share prices in London inched higher in Wall Street's wake on Thursday, marking time as voting started in Britain's general election, while the dollar sat just below a fresh multi-year high against the yen.
But trading was constrained with most of Europe's key financial markets other than London closed for the May 1 holiday and yet more vital U.S. economic indicators due later in the day and on Friday.
London shares took their cue from Wall Street's third day of gains which carried the Dow Jones Industrial Average above 7,000 for the first time in seven weeks on Wednesday.
The Dow rose 46.96 points to close at 7,008.99, a day after soaring 179 points in its second largest points gain ever.

The U.S. index is within reach of its March 11 record close of 7,085.16 and has now recaptured more than 600 of the 700 points it lost between March 11 and April 11 on worries over corporate profitability and fears of higher interest rates.
"This market truly has been manic-depressive in the last six weeks," U.S.-based Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd, said of Wall Street.

Another U.S. economic statistic will keep stock traders on the edge of their seats on both sides of the Atlantic on Thursday. The National Association of Purchasing Management's manufacturing index for April, due out at 1400 GMT, is expected to fall to 53.6 from 55.0 in March, according to a Reuters poll.
The U.S. April jobs report due on Friday is among those the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank watches closely in gauging inflation pressures.

Global financial markets are highly sensitive to U.S. economic statistics as investors try to guess whether the Federal Open Market Committee, the central bank's policy arm, will raise interest rates again when it meets on May 20. It nudged a key short-term rate up by a quarter point on March 25 to counter inflationary pressures.
London's FTSE index of blue chip shares was up 4.6 points at 4,440.6 at around 0930 GMT in gentle trade, although prices were unexpectedly squeezed higher after a mixed opening.
"The market will find it very difficult to make much progress now the election is upon us," said one trader. "Despite the fact that Wall Street was up...it will be a very dull day."
Britain's monetary authorities are due to meet next Wednesday to discuss policy but dealers said they did not expect a rate rise so soon after the election.
Politics is likely to dominate the rest of the day and the latest opinion polls continue to forecast a resounding victory for the opposition Labour party after 18 years of Conservative rule.
The polls have consistently shown Labour to be well ahead in the race and dealers said a Labour win was already factored into prices. "Thoughts are turned now to the size of the majority," one said.

In currencies, the dollar sat just below a fresh multi-year high against the yen at the start of European trade, its sentiment buoyed by a series of strong U.S. economic data and a rise in U.S. asset markets on Wednesday.
However the dollar's energy, which pushed it to a 55-month high against the yen in the Asian session, was ebbing slightly as most European markets were closed for the May 1 holiday.

"Dollar/yen seems to be losing momentum at the mid-127 level, partially because of a holiday in a large part of Europe and also because of U.S. figures again today and tomorrow," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.
"Also, the market has grown increasingly aware of worries about Bank of Japan intervention in the mid-127 (yen) area, so we shouldn't expect further gains from here," Demolli said.

The dollar was at 127.36 yen at 0750 GMT after hitting 127.45 yen earlier, according to Bank of Japan data, its highest since August 1992. Dollar/yen was at 126.95 in late European trade on Wednesday.

It was at 1.7321 marks against 1.7216 late on Wednesday. Analysts said that with European trading expected to be quiet this morning, dollar/mark was unlikely to challenge the 37-month high of 1.7375 it reached last month.

Meanwhile, the pound made a firm start against the dollar and mark, although it was stuck in a range as the market awaited the election results after the markets close. It was trading at about 1.6266 dollars compared with 1.6225 late on Wednesday.
STOCKS AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 4.6 points or 0.1 percent at 4,440.6.
The Paris CAC-40 index was closed for the May 1 holiday after finishing up 36.60 points on Wednesday at 2,639.46.
Frankfurt's DAX index was also closed after finishing up 54.88 points at 3,474.98 on Wednesday.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7290 marks compared with 1.7312 marks in late European trade on Wednesday. It was at 127.30 yen compared with 126.93 late on Wednesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $339.55 compared with Wednesday's close of $339.65 an ounce in London.
